deliberation: The revised candidate resolves several round-one topology defects: every phase now names declared gates, T0 is the non-retrospective successful protected-main activation-readback timestamp, OPS-A is stated as a hard predecessor, and the primary observation interval ends at T0 plus P8DT4H48M with PT19H12M reserved before P9D. The declared MATH-PROGRAMME commit, plan blob and SHA-256, and transform-manifest blob and SHA-256 reproduce exactly, and the three candidate transform tests pass. The dependency repair is not yet executable, however. The validator reads only the transform manifest; it does not read the plan, enumerate workstream gates, encode predecessors, or reject an unknown phase-exit gate, a missing terminal node, a cycle, or a predecessor whose deadline is later than its dependent. Thus it cannot enforce either the repaired phase map or the OPS-A barrier and does not satisfy the round-one machine-check condition. The terminal path also remains ambiguous: ADM-03 says to issue a reliability disposition at the end of the observation window, ADM-B permits terminal receipts and readbacks through P9D, and the Phase 3 exit omits ADM-03. A late-but-valid closeout inside the reserved buffer can therefore occur after the stated disposition point, with no declared cutoff-snapshot to ADM-B to ADM-03 to consolidated-packet order. T0 itself is now temporally sound, but no activation-receipt contract binds and distinguishes candidate commit, protected merge commit, protected-main readback repository/branch/head, ancestry result, plan identities, Council compilation, Human Steward disposition, and readback timestamp. Likewise, OPS-00 names five protected heads but does not require each baseline identity to be a repository/branch/SHA/observed-at/readback-evidence tuple. These omissions matter precisely because merge identity and later protected heads need not equal the reviewed candidate and because all five repositories may move independently. The exact nine-day schedule is therefore reviewable in prose but not yet a fail-closed executable dependency map.
discharged_obligations: Reconstructed the activation, protected merge, protected-main readback, T0, OPS baseline, downstream workstream, observation-cutoff, terminalization, disposition, and consolidated-review dependency paths.
Checked every phase-exit gate reference against the workstream register and compared its declared deadline with the integrated milestone schedule.
Reassessed each round-one Cartographer condition against the exact revised MATH-PROGRAMME candidate rather than treating the correction summary as evidence of discharge.
Verified the exact candidate commit, plan blob and file digest, transform-manifest blob and file digest, and successful candidate transform tests.
Assessed identity drift across reviewed candidate, protected merge commit, protected-main readback head, and the five-repository OPS-00 baseline.
findings: The phase table now references only declared canonical workstream gates, and the PT4H48M, P2DT12H, P5DT9H36M, P8DT4H48M, and P9D offsets are arithmetically coherent.
T0 is now defined after successful protected-main activation readback, so merge-to-readback latency no longer consumes the active nine-day window retrospectively.
The plan states OPS-A as a hard predecessor and permits only OPS-00 construction and verification evidence before it, materially correcting the prior unbound downstream-start risk.

The transform validator validates internal duration arithmetic and the presence of eight noncompressed-requirement labels, but it does not consume the plan or any machine-readable gate/dependency graph; it therefore cannot reject unknown gate references, deadline inversions, cycles, missing predecessors, or violation of the OPS-A barrier.

The observation cutoff now precedes P9D by PT19H12M, but ADM-03 is placed at the end of the observation window while ADM-B allows terminalization through P9D, and ADM-03 is absent from the Phase 3 exit condition; the closeout order is not deterministic.

The candidate does not define a durable activation-receipt schema or artifact that distinguishes candidate head, protected merge commit, protected-main readback head, ancestry result, and readback time while binding the plan, Council compilation, and Human Steward disposition identities.

OPS-00 requires protected heads and active contracts for five repositories, but cross-repository baseline identity is not specified as repository plus protected branch plus commit plus observation timestamp plus canonical readback evidence; a bare head value is insufficient to reconstruct a moving multi-repository cut.

The manifest names a source plan ID and copies source durations but binds no exact predecessor repository, commit, path, blob, or SHA-256, so successful validation proves arithmetic over self-declared source seconds rather than an exact transform of an independently identified predecessor artifact.
conditions: Add a machine-readable gate and dependency schedule, and make validation reject unknown or duplicate gate IDs, missing phase-exit nodes, cycles, predecessor deadlines later than dependent deadlines, and any downstream workstream node reachable before successful OPS-A; validation must bind that schedule to the exact plan candidate.

Define and validate the terminal chain as observation cutoff, durable cutoff snapshot, per-occurrence terminal receipt/readback or preserved cutoff state, ADM-B, ADM-03 reliability disposition, and consolidated terminal packet, with explicit deadlines inside the PT19H12M reserve and retention of events completed after cutoff.

Define a fail-closed activation-receipt contract that binds the Council matter digest, compiled disposition digest, authenticated Human Steward disposition identity, candidate commit, protected merge commit, plan blob and SHA-256, protected-main repository and branch, protected-main readback head, ancestry result, merge timestamp, and readback timestamp; T0 must be created only by durable successful validation of that receipt.

Define each OPS-00 protected baseline entry as an exact repository, protected branch, commit, observed-at timestamp, and canonical readback-evidence tuple, bind active contract paths to blobs or content digests, and block only affected downstream lanes when any tuple cannot be reproduced.

Bind the transform manifest to the exact predecessor plan artifact by repository, commit, path, blob, and SHA-256, and validate the source phase, milestone, and cadence values against that bound artifact or a separately content-addressed source schedule rather than accepting self-declared source seconds alone.

Retable the resulting exact candidate and Council matter because these dependency, receipt, and provenance repairs change governed bytes and the active proposal forbids carrying this review across such a change.
residual_uncertainty: The existing maintenance cadence anchor determines how many authoritative occurrences fall inside the half-open observation interval and is not knowable until the OPS-00 baseline is captured.
PT19H12M creates a topologically usable closeout reserve, but no bounded ordinary merge, receipt, readback, or independent-compilation latency is evidenced for that reserve.

Protected heads in MATH-PROGRAMME, MATHFORGE, MATHSOLVE, MATHCERT, and INTELLECT will continue to drift between Council review, merge, activation readback, and OPS-00 and must be captured rather than presumed equal.

Availability of distinct non-author reviewers and an independent external actor within the compressed critical path remains an operational uncertainty; a blocker or continuation packet remains the honest output if they are unavailable.

Passing the candidate transform tests establishes only their covered arithmetic invariants and does not establish successful required checks, protected merge, protected-main inclusion, activation, or feasibility of every nine-day workstream.
